title: Zions Bank Employees to Brighten Up Nonprofit Preschool During 33rd Annual Paint-a-Thon
summary: Zions Bank Employees to Brighten Up Nonprofit Preschool During 33rd Annual Paint-a-Thon
body_markdown:
SALT LAKE CITY, Utah; June 2, 2025 — Zions Bank employees are trading in balance sheets for paint brushes to give a local nonprofit a makeover — one of 15 projects happening in Utah next week during the bank’s annual Paint-a-Thon.


About 75 volunteers — including Zions Bank president and CEO Paul Burdiss — will gather on Monday, June 2, at the James R. Russell Head Start Center, a preschool operated by Utah Community Action, to create a more welcoming environment for the children and families it serves.


Volunteers will spruce up the facility, including painting a shed, washing windows, landscaping and cleaning. They will also assemble information packets and distribute flyers to raise awareness for the Head Start program, a no-cost preschool for children, birth through age 5, who are experiencing poverty. The program serves more than 2,000 children each year, many of whom are experiencing homelessness or in the foster care system.


The volunteer effort is among 15 projects taking place in Utah as part of Zions Bank’s 33rd annual Paint-a-Thon, which runs from June 2-4. More than 1,100 volunteers — consisting of Zions Bank employees and their family members— will tackle projects from Brigham City to Bicknell.


From painting classrooms for the Boys and Girls Club of Northern Utah to painting exam rooms at the Wayne Community Health Center, this year’s Paint-a-Thon projects directly or indirectly benefit more than 13,000 Utahns and improve nearly 1,000 affordable or supportive housing units in Utah.


“Paint-a-Thon is a chance to give back to the nonprofits and individuals who give so much to our communities,” said Zions Bank president and CEO Paul Burdiss. “It’s one of many ways Zions Bank is focused on investing in the communities we serve.”


Launched in 1991, Zions Bank’s Paint-a-Thon began as a volunteer project for a dozen homes along Utah’s Wasatch Front. Over the past three decades, Zions Bank employees have painted 1,316 homes and nonprofit facilities throughout Utah, Idaho and Wyoming. Not counting the dollar value of volunteer hours through the years, the bank has donated more than $1.5 million toward beautifying communities in the three states.


**About Zions Bank**


Zions Bank is Utah’s oldest financial institution and is the only local bank with a statewide distribution of branches operating 93 full-service branches. Zions Bank also operates 26 branches in Idaho and Wyoming. In addition to offering a wide range of traditional banking services, Zions Bank is also a leader in small business lending. Founded in 1873, Zions Bank has been serving the communities of Utah for more than 150 years. Additional information is available at[www.zionsbank.com](https://www.zionsbank.com/) . A division of Zions Bancorporation N.A., Member FDIC.


**About Utah Community Action**


Utah Community Action’s mission is to empower individuals, strengthen families, and build communities through education and self-reliance programs. Each year, they assist over 50,000 children and families experiencing poverty through programs supporting housing stability, early childhood education, and workforce development.
